messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: exact factorscores
parts:
Luc

There are no "exact" factor scores, becuase any 1 set of factor scores is indeterminant. Meaning there can be multiple sets of factor scores that can satisfied ts conditions. To work with factor scores there is the still experimental method in lavaan, which is a 2 step method that adjust the factor scores to retain the factor relations between them. Or you could use the plausibel values approach to account for factor indeterminancy.

When you say that you dont want to have a Maximum Liklihood solution, and use VCOV. What are you looking for? What estimation method? Why you dont want to use ML? Sorry these thingas are not clear to me, and would help use to help you

With lavaan you can use different estimation methods, look the lavaan help page for more details, several of those adjust for non-normality, for categorical data, or with less assumptions. But ML would be the deault method, but you are not required to use it

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: exact factorscores
parts:
I also don't understand what you want. So, you have (somehow) computed
factor-scores F1, F2, ... Fn. And you wish to use them in a model, that
(I suppose) only contains regressions (as no measurement model is needed).

Then, you could use syntax like

model <- '

F1 ~ F2 + F3 + F4
F2 ~ F4
# and so on
'

and fit the model with

fit <- sem(model, data = yourdata).

Indeed, by default lavaan will use ML estimation. But why is that a
problem? What is 'VCOV' referring to? The variance/covariance matrix of
the observed variables? Or the vcov of the parameter estimates?

Finally, factor scores still contain measurement error. To get
'unbiased' estimates (for the regression coefficients in the model
above), you can use Croon's correction. But for this, you need
information about the measurement models.

If you give us more context, we may help you better.

Yves.

messages.author: ac612f5f279537d0
messages.subject: Re: exact factorscores
parts:
Dear Mauga

I computed determinate factorscores using an alternating least squares method. 
In any factor analysis you will find five matrices: Z, a centered datamatrix with unity length columns, U with the same order as Z, but consisting of the Unicities,   F , a matrix of factorscores, Labda wich is the loading matrix and psi, the diagonal matrix of standarddeviations of U.
in one simple equation:  

Z =  F t(L) + U psi 

Now estimate U by calculating a complete orthogonal matrix M with the smallest possible distance to Z. Use M to estimate U
Next , compute F by using any factorextraction. 
Next , compute Labda as t(Z) F 
Next , compute PSI just as  1 - Labda t(Labda)
You can iterate this by minimalising: U psi

The resulting F is a latent variable and an exact factorscore. 
Just multiply F with (n - 1) / sqrt(n-1) and you get "conventional factorscores with standarddeviation of 1
My problem is the following : I created oblique ( coorelated) exact factoscores and to plug these into lavaan. 
I definetely do not want to reinvent the wheel

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: exact factorscores
parts:
Not sure what you mean by "unity length." But factors are on an arbitrary metric, so you could use whatever SD you want. And SEM by design uses a variance-covariance matrix "under the hood." You haven't indicated why you wouldn't want that.

You also haven't told us your content area, but it's rarely going to be the case that important variables are perfectly orthogonal in any real-world setting, so I'd suggest using one of the oblique cases.

Frankly, you're not giving us a lot to work with to try to help.

Pat

parts:
Luc

I have never seen the term "exact factor scores", any set of factor scores are approximations which can lead to issues.
The main ways to use factor scores and correct for this is eaither use the Croons corection or plausible vaues methods.
What you presented is one method to calculate the factor scores from a factor model, which would be similar to use a set of predicted factor scores from lavaan.
ALso, if you extract factor scores from an orthogonal model, and then do an alayis swith them, by default they will have 0 relations

As lavaan does SEM, it is a sufficient/limited information meaning that it will (by default) transformed the data set you provide into the variance/covariance matrix. And this matrix is used a the observed data for estimation. So, you can provide the factor scores matrix, or the covariance matrix between them. In any case lavaan wil end up using the same covariance matrix as it transform it before analysis.

It seems you are looking for a full information method that doesnt use sufficient/limited information. In lavaan you can do this with the estimator MML (Marginal Maximum Likelihood). There are other programs that will have other full information methods

-- Mauricio

You also haven't told us your content area, but it's rarely going to be the case that important variables are perfectly orthogonal in any real-world setting, so I'd suggest using one of the oblique cases.

Dear Mauga

I computed determinate factorscores using an alternating least squares method. 
In any factor analysis you will find five matrices: Z, a centered datamatrix with unity length columns, U with the same order as Z, but consisting of the Unicities,   F , a matrix of factorscores, Labda wich is the loading matrix and psi, the diagonal matrix of standarddeviations of U.
in one simple equation:  

Z =  F t(L) + U psi 

Now estimate U by calculating a complete orthogonal matrix M with the smallest possible distance to Z. Use M to estimate U
Next , compute F by using any factorextraction. 
Next , compute Labda as t(Z) F 
Next , compute PSI just as  1 - Labda t(Labda)
You can iterate this by minimalising: U psi

The resulting F is a latent variable and an exact factorscore. 
Just multiply F with (n - 1) / sqrt(n-1) and you get "conventional factorscores with standarddeviation of 1

Luc

There are no "exact" factor scores, becuase any 1 set of factor scores is indeterminant. Meaning there can be multiple sets of factor scores that can satisfied ts conditions. To work with factor scores there is the still experimental method in lavaan, which is a 2 step method that adjust the factor scores to retain the factor relations between them. Or you could use the plausibel values approach to account for factor indeterminancy.

When you say that you dont want to have a Maximum Liklihood solution, and use VCOV. What are you looking for? What estimation method? Why you dont want to use ML? Sorry these thingas are not clear to me, and would help use to help you

With lavaan you can use different estimation methods, look the lavaan help page for more details, several of those adjust for non-normality, for categorical data, or with less assumptions. But ML would be the deault method, but you are not required to use it
